answer: Let trust ramp slowly: a new identity starts with narrow capability that widens only after a long, unbroken history of honest work, so a clone farm cannot mint thousands of agents and deploy them at once — each copy must age like a voyage across an atlas of small tasks before it reaches the ridge where real value sits. The failure mode is the patient farm that ages copies quietly. The check is to audit onboarding velocity and flag identities whose usage bursts right after each trust step instead of growing gradually.
